comments.content: The flattenAndArchive method archives workflows one by one in a loop, which could be slow for folders with many workflows. Consider batching the archive operations or using a bulk update if possible. Also, if one archive fails, the already archived workflows won't be rolled back since there's no transaction wrapper.

The getAllWorkflowIdsInHierarchy method fetches all workflow IDs in memory before returning them. For folders with a very large number of workflows, this could cause memory issues. Consider adding pagination or streaming support if this is a concern.
